titulo: If I had time, I would travel
intro: A real condition uses the present; an imagined condition uses the imperfect subjunctive and the conditional.
p.si.consejo: With an imagined condition, the conditional does not follow «si»: you say «si tuviera», not «si tendría».
p.tuviera.consejo: It comes from «tuvieron»: change «-ron» to «-ra». It looks like past, but it speaks of something not real now.
p.fuera.consejo: It works for «ser» and «ir», because both make «fueron»: «si yo fuera tú», «si fuera a Roma».
p.viajaría.consejo: Infinitive plus «-ía»: «viajar» + «ía». The v sounds like b and the j sounds like h.
p.hablaría.consejo: It is «hablar» plus «-ía». The initial h is silent: it sounds a-bla-RÍ-a.
p.tendría.consejo: It is irregular: not «tener» + «ía», but «tendr-». Compare «tendré» and «tendría».
p.tiempo.consejo: It also means weather: «hace buen tiempo». For free time you say «tengo tiempo» or «no tengo tiempo».
p.dinero.consejo: It is almost always singular: «mucho dinero», «poco dinero». The stress falls on «ne»: di-NE-ro.
p.lotería.consejo: The accent on «í» separates the vowels: lo-te-RÍ-a has four syllables.
p.imaginar.consejo: It comes from «imagen». The g before i sounds like h: i-ma-hi-NAR.
p.compraría.consejo: A regular verb: «comprar» + «ía». All singular persons sound the same: compraría.
p.agencia.consejo: At an «agencia de viajes» they help you plan a trip. The c sounds like th: a-HEN-thya.
b1.texto:
When something is **possible**, you speak in the present:

- **Si tengo** tiempo, voy al cine.

When you only **imagine** it, the verb changes form:

- **Si tuviera** tiempo, **viajaría**.
- **Si yo fuera** tú, **hablaría** con ella.

The part with **si** takes the **imperfect subjunctive** (tuviera, fuera). The result takes the **conditional** (viajaría, hablaría).
b2.f0.texto: What are you doing in August?
b2.f1.texto: If I have time, I go to Granada with my sister.
b2.f2.texto: If I had time, I would travel all over Europe.
b2.f3.texto: And what would you do with a lot of money?
b2.f4.texto: If I had a lot of money, I would buy a house by the sea.
b2.f5.texto: I would not buy anything and I would travel all year.
b2.f6.texto: If I were you, I would talk to a travel agency.
b2.f7.texto: First I need to win the lottery.
b4.texto:
There are two patterns for the present and the future:

- Possible: **si + present**, then present, future or command. Si estudias, aprobarás.
- Imagined: **si + imperfect subjunctive**, then **conditional**. Si estudiaras, aprobarías.

The **conditional** is the infinitive plus **-ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -íais, -ían**: hablar → hablaría, comer → comería, vivir → viviría.

Some verbs change their stem: tener → **tendría**, hacer → **haría**, poder → **podría**, decir → **diría**.

After an imagined **si** the conditional never appears: «si tendría» is a mistake.
b4.e0.texto: If I have time, I go to the cinema.
b4.e1.texto: If I had time, I would go to the cinema.
b4.e2.texto: If you studied more, you would pass the exam.
b5.f0.texto: In grandfather's drawer sleeps a yellow map of faraway cities.
b5.f1.texto: Lucía unfolds it on the table with trembling fingers.
b5.f2.texto: The blue lines of the rivers shine under the lamp like threads of water.
b5.f3.texto: Each strange name promises her a different afternoon and a new smell.
b5.f4.texto: For an instant, the room smells of sea, of warm bread and of wet earth.
b5.f5.texto: If she had time, Lucía would follow the red road to the coast.
b5.f6.texto: She would sleep in white villages and drink fresh water from the fountains.
b5.f7.texto: If she were braver, she would leave that very night with a light backpack.
b5.f8.texto: Today she folds the map very carefully and puts it away under the books.
b5.f9.texto: The light of the lamp trembles for a moment on the old paper.
b6.o0.refuerzo: «Tengo» is present: the condition is possible, not imagined.
b6.o1.refuerzo: Yes! «Tuviera» and «viajaría» mark something that is not real now.
b6.o2.refuerzo: It is a real habit: «cuando» and present, nothing imagined.
b6.pregunta: Which sentence speaks of something only imagined?
b7.o0.refuerzo: «Viajaré» is future and goes with a real condition, not an imagined one.
b7.o1.refuerzo: Exactly: the result of an imagined condition is the conditional.
b7.o2.refuerzo: It is subjunctive: it works after «si», not for the result.
b7.pregunta: It is an imagined trip. Which form is missing?
b8.frase: Si yo fuera tú, hablaría con ella
b8.traduccion: If I were you, I would talk to her
b9.frase: Si yo ____ tú, hablaría con ella.
b9.o0.refuerzo: Correct: an imagined condition asks for the imperfect subjunctive.
b9.o1.refuerzo: «Era» is indicative and speaks of a real fact in the past.
b9.o2.refuerzo: «Sería» is conditional: it cannot follow an imagined «si».
b9.pregunta: You are not the other person. Which form is missing?
b10.o0: Si tuviera dinero, compraría una casa.
b10.o0.refuerzo: It is right: imperfect subjunctive and conditional.
b10.o1: Si tendría dinero, compraría una casa.
b10.o1.refuerzo: That's it! After «si» you do not use «tendría», but «tuviera».
b10.o2.refuerzo: It is right: «fuera» and «viajaría» go together.
b10.pregunta: Which of these sentences is wrong?
b11.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «If I had money, I would travel.»
b12.o0.refuerzo: Well done: a real condition uses the present.
b12.o1.refuerzo: «Tuviera» imagines something unreal; here the condition is possible.
b12.o2.refuerzo: «Tendría» is conditional and does not follow «si».
b12.pregunta: It is possible and real. Which form is missing?
p.iría.consejo: From «ir» plus «-ía». Although «ir» is irregular in the present, its conditional is regular.
p.estudiaras.consejo: From «estudiaron»: drop «-ron», add «-ras». It is the imperfect subjunctive for tú.
p.aprobarías.consejo: Conditional of «aprobar» for tú. The accent on «í» separates the vowels: a-pro-ba-RÍ-as.
p.cajón.consejo: It is masculine and the j sounds like h. It comes from «caja» plus the ending «-ón».
p.abuelo.consejo: Its feminine is «abuela». It is written with b and the «ue» sounds like one beat: a-BWE-lo.
p.despliega.consejo: From «desplegar»: the e becomes «ie» in the singular. It is the opposite of «plegar».
p.temblorosos.consejo: It comes from «temblar» and ends in «-oso». It agrees with «dedos»: masculine plural.
p.líneas.consejo: It is feminine plural. It stresses the first syllable, so it carries an accent: LÍ-ne-as.
p.ríos.consejo: Plural of «río». The accent on «í» keeps the two vowels apart: RRÍ-os.
p.hilos.consejo: Plural of «hilo». The initial h is silent: I-los.
p.extraño.consejo: It means unusual or unknown. The ñ sounds like ny and the x like ks: eks-TRA-nyo.
p.promete.consejo: From «prometer»: it is regular. The stress falls on «me»: pro-ME-te.
p.distinta.consejo: Feminine of «distinto». It agrees with «tarde»: «una tarde distinta».
p.instante.consejo: A very short moment. It is masculine: «un instante». The stress falls on «tan».
p.seguiría.consejo: Conditional of «seguir». The u is silent: «gui» sounds like «gi»: se-gi-RÍ-a.
p.dormiría.consejo: Conditional of «dormir»: infinitive plus «-ía». The o does not change here.
p.pueblos.consejo: Plural of «pueblo»: a small place where people live. The «ue» sounds like PWE.
p.blancos.consejo: Masculine plural of «blanco». It agrees with «pueblos».
p.bebería.consejo: Conditional of «beber»: infinitive plus «-ía». It has four syllables: be-be-RÍ-a.
p.fuentes.consejo: Plural of «fuente». It can be a natural spring or a square with water. The «ue» sounds FWE.
p.saldría.consejo: Irregular conditional of «salir»: it adds a d, «saldr-», like «saldré».
p.mochila.consejo: A bag carried on the back. The ch sounds as in «chocolate»: mo-CHI-la.
p.dobla.consejo: From «doblar»: to fold something. It also means to turn at a corner.
p.tiembla.consejo: From «temblar»: the e becomes «ie» in yo, tú, él and ellos: «tiembla».
